newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's Van Miert has strong doubts about Boeing deal.
newsitem.headline: EU's Van Miert has strong doubts about Boeing deal.

text.p: BRUSSELS, May 13 (reuter) - European Union Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert expressed serious doubts about the legality under European competition rules of the Boeing/McDonnell Douglas merger on Tuesday and said he expected the companies to offer formal remedies to his worries.

"As a consequence of our strong doubts, we have decided to initiate an in-depth scrutiny into this merger file... because we expressed very serious reservations as to the compatibility of the proposed merger with the European rules on competition policy," he said in a statement.
"The initiation of such an in-depth inquiry clearly demonstrates that, in its present form, this merger case is not in line with the European merger regulation," Van Miert said.
The deadline for the Commission's decision on whether to clear the deal is on July 31. Van Miert said he expected a so called statement of objections to be ready before end-May.
"In this document which will be sent to the companies involved in this merger case, we will clearly point out all the elements that cause our deep worries," he said.
"As usual we expect the recipient companies to offer formal remedies to the worries expressed," Van Miert added.
The Commission began its in-depth probe on March 13.
Van Miert also reacted to press reports that some members of the U.S. senate took the view that the Commission's approach to the merger was "politically motivated".
Van Miert strongly disputed this, saying the analysis was based on facts and figures and not on 'political issues'.
"Our analysis of the Boeing-McDonnell Douglas file is conducted strictly on the basis of the European merger regulation, and nothing else," he said.

When launching the probe in March the Commission said it would in particular have to examine to what extent Boeing's leading position in the market for commercial jet aircraft could be strengthened by the merger.

Van Miert has also expressed concern about the greater leverage the group would have in negotiating exclusive contracts with airlines, following Boeing deals agreed by Delta Air Lines and AMR Corp.'s American Airlines.
The alliance is also being investigated by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission.
